title: What Home Health Aides Do
description: Home health aides help elderly, disabled, and recovering people live at home: bathing, dressing, and grooming assistance, light housekeeping, meal preparation, medication reminders, and companionship. They work under nurse supervision for agencies or directly for families — the hands and heart of home care.
how_it_works: Follow the care plan each visit
requirements: High school diploma; state training requirements vary
75+ hours training for Medicare-certified agencies (federal minimum)
standards: Dignity and privacy in all personal care
safety: Fall prevention in the home
Safe transfer and mobility assistance
Medication reminders only — never administer beyond scope
Report changes in condition to the nurse promptly
troubleshooting: Client refuses care: respect, redirect, report
Family conflict: stay neutral, document, escalate
Emergency: call 911, then agency protocol
Burnout: use respite and support resources
citations: Home-care training curricula; federal home health aide training requirements; caregiving professional references.
